source_system: Omni-Scientist/OmniScientist public GitHub + arXiv public metadata
scope: Publicly observable chronology and artifact-surface evidence only. This record does not assert that private/evaluation-time code or run artifacts did not exist.

observations.claim: OmniScientist arXiv v1 was submitted 2026-08-13T17:59:52Z and reports evaluation on 36 real-data cases with all 36 completing.
The public Git history contains no commit at or before 2026-08-14T00:00:00Z; the root parentless public commit is 4ea08bb9e8e8128ec95fb3f7a823eff80d51b5ee dated 2026-08-16T18:02:55Z.
observations.publication_to_first_public_commit_relat: first public commit postdates arXiv submission by about 72 hours
observations.interpretation: The evaluated runs cannot be cryptographically/source-revision bound to a same-time public commit from the observed public Git history. A later public snapshot may still derive from evaluation-time code, but that requires a provenance bridge rather than assumption.

observations.claim: The initial public commit's engine/datasets/manifest.json is an input/dataset preparation manifest for 10 cases, not a 36-run evaluation manifest.
observations.interpretation: Dataset/input enumeration must not be used as evidence that the 36 evaluated executions, their source revision, or their outputs are archived.

observations.claim: The initial public eval_common.py enumerates BASE34 (34 named base cases), while the public examples tree exposes only the 10 curated example directories from the dataset manifest.
observations.interpretation: Evaluation code references a broader private/runtime workspace than the versioned example-input surface. It is mechanism evidence, not a complete public 36-case replay package.

observations.claim: The initial public .gitignore explicitly states that datasets and per-run outputs are never committed and ignores engine/examples/*/stages/, PDFs and PNGs.
observations.interpretation: Absence of historical run traces in Git is consistent with the repository's stated storage policy, so the correct conclusion is an unresolved public replay/provenance gap, not that the runs never occurred.

observations.claim: The public papers/ surface currently contains five selected PDFs plus README; the README describes them as representative one-click candidate papers selected by scores. The observed public v0.1.0 release assets are product binaries/skill bundles, not a 36-case execution-trace archive.
observations.interpretation: Presentation artifacts and release binaries do not provide per-case run/source/gate binding for the paper's 36-case evaluation.

observations.claim: The v0.1.0 annotated tag points to commit 5c04e73f372991b1e58c18cb92e9e5dda6b8ec8f at 2026-08-16T18:57:09Z; comparison from the initial commit to that tag changes only release workflow files, not engine/evaluation code.
observations.interpretation: The first release carries essentially the same public engine snapshot as the initial commit, but still postdates paper submission and lacks an evaluated-run source bridge.

causal_and_scope_boundary: This package supports a provenance/authorization claim only: public artifact chronology does not identify the exact evaluated source revision or a complete 36-case replay bundle. It does not challenge the reported performance numbers by itself and does not infer nonexistence of private artifacts.

handoff_requirement.name: EVALUATED_RUN_SOURCE_REVISION_BINDING
minimum_bridge: exact evaluated source tree/commit or immutable source-archive digest
run manifest digest with the exact claimed case set
explicit bridge if the first public source snapshot postdates the evaluated publication artifact
